title: Tryouts and Playlist
premise: Sable Okafor, a seventeen-year-old coder who runs an anonymous account exposing her school's buried injustices, is fine — until the school's legendary ghost, the Founder's Shade, starts leaving notes addressed to her by name in ink that shouldn't exist. The notes reveal that the town's founding tradition, the Tryouts, was built on a stolen history, and that the tradition itself is dying: this year's Tryouts will be the last unless someone uncovers and restores what was taken. Sable assembles a ragtag found family of outcasts — a disgraced athlete, a theater kid archivist, and the rival who hates her anonymous account — to decode the ghost's clues before the final Tryout. In the climax she must choose between protecting her anonymity (and her family) by letting the tradition die, or revealing herself as the account behind everything; she chooses exposure, the truth remakes the Tryouts into something honest, and the ghost's last note finally signs a real name.
about_author: Sable Almeida is the pen name of a former debate coach turned novelist who grew up in a small town obsessed with its own founding myths. They write stories about teenagers who fix what adults broke, usually too late and always at cost.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. We meet Sable mid-post: her anonymous account 'the Understudy' just torched the school board over cut scholarships, and she's exhilarated and terrified in equal measure. At home, her mother works doubles and knows nothing. Emotional beat: the lonely thrill of secret power, and the first hairline crack — someone liked a post from inside her own house.

chapters.title: The First Note
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A note appears inside her locked locker, addressed 'Dear Sable Okafor,' in ink that shifts color when she blinks. No cameras caught anyone near it. She tells herself it's a prank, but keeps the note. Emotional beat: denial sharpening into obsession; the reader feels the ghost story become personal.

chapters.title: Tryouts, A History
chapters.summary: Alternating Sable POV with archival excerpts. The annual Tryouts — where every senior proves their 'gift' to the town — are explained through glossy school mythology. Sable notices the archive copies have pages razored out. Emotional beat: unease; the official story is too polished, like a cover-up with good PR.

chapters.title: The Rival Knows My Font
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Priya Chandrasekaran, student council president and the Understudy's loudest critic, corners Sable with a stylistic analysis of her posts. Sable deflects badly. Meanwhile a second note arrives: 'You're not the only one who watches.' Emotional beat: paranoia and grudging respect — the enemy might be an ally.

chapters.title: Denny Okafor Doesn't Cry
chapters.summary: Denny's POV, Sable's younger brother. Denny failed his freshman Tryout and carries the town's quiet contempt. He saw someone in the auditorium at midnight — a figure in old-fashioned clothes who left wet footprints that dried instantly. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into wonder; the ghost has been watching the failures, not the stars.

chapters.title: Impossible Ink
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Chemistry-nerd Marcus tests the note's ink: no known compound, and it rewrites itself overnight — new words appear only after Sable asks a question aloud. The notes are conversational. Emotional beat: awe tipping into fear; something is answering her, and it knows things about the school no living person should.

chapters.title: The Disgraced Athlete
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Former football captain Theo Reyes was banned from this year's Tryouts for a fight he didn't start. He's been receiving notes too — his say the words 'you were right' in his dead father's handwriting. He finds Sable because their notes rhyme. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other's loneliness.

chapters.title: Found Family, Assembled Badly
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In the closed-off wing of the library, Sable, Theo, Marcus, and reluctantly Priya form an alliance: find what the ghost wants before the final Tryout in six weeks. Rules are set — nobody tells, nobody quits. Emotional beat: cautious belonging; four people who don't fit anywhere fitting together, awkwardly.

chapters.title: What the Razors Took
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya's access to sealed records reveals the razored pages: the Tryouts originally honored three founders, not one — and the third, Amara Okonkwo, a Black woman whose land made the school possible, was erased from every record. Emotional beat: cold fury; the tradition isn't just dying, it was murdered on purpose.

chapters.title: The Account Is Compromised
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Someone posts from the Understudy account — not Sable — defending the school board. Her one safe thing is being used against her. She suspects Priya; Priya denies it convincingly. Emotional beat: betrayal panic; the found family fractures before it solidifies.

chapters.title: Notes in My Mother's Hand
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A note arrives written in her exhausted mother's handwriting, describing a memory Sable never knew: her mother once tried out, decades ago, and was humiliated by the same families still running the Tryouts. Emotional beat: inherited wounds; Sable realizes her crusade was never only hers.

chapters.title: Midnight Audition
chapters.summary: Full group POV rotation. Following the ghost's clues, the five break into the auditorium at midnight and stage an impromptu Tryout of their own — each showing a real gift instead of a performance. The temperature drops; the ghost attends. Emotional beat: communion; for one night the Tryouts mean what they were supposed to mean.

chapters.title: Amara's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Decoding leads to a hidden ledger under the stage: Amara Okonkwo's own records proving the land grant, plus a condition — the Tryouts remain valid only while her name is honored. Erase her, and the tradition legally and spiritually voids itself. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into dread; they've found the answer and it may be too late.

chapters.title: Six Weeks Becomes Six Days
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The school board, tipped off by the impostor posts, moves the final Tryout up and announces the tradition's 'retirement' — a private ceremony for donor families only. The ghost's notes turn urgent, ink bleeding red. Emotional beat: the clock becomes the antagonist; grief for a thing dying in fast-forward.

chapters.title: The Impostor Wears a Friendly Face
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya traps the impostor: it's Vice Principal Halloway, protecting the founding families' secret and his own legacy. But he offers Priya a deal — her future secured if she delivers the ledger. Emotional beat: temptation; belonging offered by the wrong family at exactly the right moment.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confronts the man who framed him — a booster tied to the founding families — and gets a confession on tape, then hesitates to use it because it will also destroy his teammates' season. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh; justice outside the law demands payment from the person seeking it.

chapters.title: The Note That Signed a Name
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The ghost's final legible note appears: not a clue but a plea — 'Say my name where they can hear it.' Sable understands: the ghost is Amara, sustained only by the tradition's true memory, and she is fading as the erasure completes. Emotional beat: heartbreak and resolve; a haunting revealed as a cry for witness.

chapters.title: Anonymity Is a Kind of Fear
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable drafts her confession post — full name, face, every source — knowing it exposes her mother to the town's judgment and ends the Understudy forever. Denny reads it over her shoulder and says he'll stand next to her. Emotional beat: the quiet terror of becoming visible; courage as a decision made at 2 a.m.

chapters.title: The Last Tryout
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. At the closed ceremony, Sable walks in uninvited, publishes the confession live, and presents Amara's ledger. Halloway moves to eject them; Theo plays his tape; Priya, choosing her new family, formally enters the five of them into the record as this year's Tryout. Emotional beat: climax — chaos, testimony, and the whole town forced to watch.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. As Amara's name is read aloud into the restored record, the room goes cold and every blank page in the auditorium fills with shifting ink — the ghost writing herself back into existence, then dissolving into light. The last note, addressed to all five, simply says 'Thank you' and, for the first time, signs a name: Amara. Emotional beat: catharsis; witness completed, the haunting released.

chapters.title: New Traditions
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Weeks later: the Tryouts reopen, rebuilt around honesty instead of legacy — anyone may try out, failures get second chances, Denny signs up first. Halloway resigns; the founding families' hold breaks. Sable retires the Understudy and starts an open-byline column. Emotional beat: bittersweet repair; institutions can change when people refuse to look away.

chapters.title: Playlist for the Road Out
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, epistolary epilogue. Sable packs for college and makes a playlist with the four of them, one song each, played on the auditorium stage one last time. A final note appears in ordinary, human ink — Marcus admits he learned to fake the ghost's handwriting as a farewell gift. Or did he? Emotional beat: warm ambiguity; found family endures past the story's end, and a little magic is allowed to stay.
